shown.chose: mutation-check the cli.ts generator-guard line itself for the alias bypass
shown.because: no writing command currently declares an alias — resolve, the only one in the registry, writes nothing — so reverting cli.ts to `c.name === cmd` leaves the suite green no matter what oracle is written. Inventing an alias on a generator purely to make a witness would change the public command surface to test it. Answered by moving the flag read behind commandFor(), which IS mutation-checked (collapse it to a name-only match and the registry oracle reds), and by enumerating the generator-refusal oracle from dispatchTokens() so an alias inherits the demand the day one exists.

shown.chose: could not dogfood either new instrument on the coherence repo itself
shown.because: coherence carries no *.spec.md and no coherence.config.json of its own, so 'verify --fast' here reports 'claims: 0' (an empty cost vector, correctly below the floor and silent) and 'atlas' reports 'no atlas config — nothing to render'. Both features were instead exercised on a purpose-built vitest project with real git history, which is also what discriminated the duration conjecture: cost printed 3.2s over 5 claims with four 800ms report-sourced rows and one 2ms wall-sourced typecheck; atlas printed 'heat █ 75%' for two crossings defined in a file touched by 3 of 4 considered commits, and the panel drew 'energy  cost 3.2s · top 804ms Dogfood  |  heat ██ mintToken 75%'.

shown.chose: batching node:test consumers — no derivable format shipped in v0.17.0, so node:test is RECOGNIZED and refused with instructions rather than guessed at
shown.because: measured on Node 25.2.1: node:test ships NO json reporter (node:test/reporters exports only default, dot, junit, lcov, spec, tap), so there is no report with a vitest-style concatenated fullName to read. Worse, its --test-name-pattern does NOT match a concatenated name — pattern 'outer group inner leaf' matched nothing while 'inner leaf' and 'outer group' each matched — so the vitest mirror (literal substring over fullName) would be WRONG for node:test, not merely unavailable. Parsing tap (nested sub-TAP) or junit (XML) is possible but the matching rule is a second semantic model, and shipping a mirror I have not verified is the one thing this feature is not allowed to do.

shown.chose: did not fix stopReport's 'in this repo' wording, which names the parent's cwd rather than the subagent's working repo
shown.because: it is a real defect (d-a50185c8/d-9ed648e4 has the evidence) but it is outside the task I was given — the command registry — and a hook-message change alters what every agent in every consuming project reads at stop time. That deserves its own pass, with a decision about whether the right fix is wording ('in <repo>' naming the resolved root) or scope (report on the cwd the agent actually worked in, which the hook cannot know). Reproduction: run any subagent whose cwd differs from its parent's; the stop report's counts describe the parent's journal.

shown.chose: verify that agents actually reach for `coherence conjecture` unprompted
shown.because: it needs a real multi-agent fan-out with the instruction line present vs absent, counted over conjecture writes per session. Everything shipped here is mechanism; whether the verb gets USED is a behavioural question this worktree cannot answer. Logged as the open conjecture d-04198572 with its discriminating test.

shown.chose: Scan JSON (package.json/lockfiles/config files) for duplicated domains
shown.because: A live instance sat in this very repo the whole time: package-lock.json said version 0.9.0 while package.json said 0.12.0 -- one fact, two spellings, disagreeing. The detector cannot see it because it reads TS and markdown only. Not built because JSON key sets are dominated by structural vocabulary (dependencies, scripts, name, version) and would need a different rarity model to avoid drowning the report; guessing at one late in the pass would have cost the precision number the whole command is judged on.

shown.chose: A derivable-bound arm: checking a computed statistic against a bound the tool could derive (4,237 removed lines attributed to a 1,139-line file)
shown.because: That is a RUNTIME consistency check over numbers a tool produced, not a static property of source text. It needs an instrumented producer that declares its own bounds (a diff stat cannot exceed the file's line count) -- a different mechanism from anything in this module, closer to a contract on a computation than to duplicate-domain detection. Building a weak static approximation would have made the command mean two unrelated things. Named here so the next agent does not assume 'redundancy' already covers it.

shown.chose: PREMISE ROT: a journaled decision can state a premise that later work invalidates, and nothing in the harness detects it. Found live in hoist: app.spec.md filed the paths invariants at root because 'the feature has no single node — the store and the wire composition live in the Patient DO and worker.ts respectively'; the capability extraction moved the store, tools and declaration into shared/paths, dissolving that premise, and the decision now reads as current guidance with a false reason. The journal is append-only and self-correcting for RETRACTED decisions, but has no mechanism for decisions whose stated reason silently expired
couldBe: the instrument is wrong — the thing that PRODUCED this number, not the thing it describes

a real and detectable advisory class: many premises name structural facts a graph already holds (a file path, 'lives in X', 'has no single node', 'confined to Y', a symbol name) — a scanner could extract path/symbol-shaped tokens from --because text and flag entries whose referents no longer exist or moved
undetectable in general: most premises are semantic, not structural, and a scanner that only catches path-shaped ones would give false confidence that the rest were checked
shown.discriminatedBy: extract path/symbol tokens from every --because in hoist's 160-entry journal, resolve each against the current graph, and hand-classify the hits: if a meaningful fraction are genuinely rotted (not just moved-but-equivalent), the advisory is real; if it is mostly noise or only ever finds the one case we already know, it is not worth building

shown.chose: the genetics frame predicts two instruments coherence lacks: (1) LOCALIZED growth-without-anchoring — a component whose mass grows while its claim count stays flat is the software analogue of a tumor (local fitness, global lethality), which the existing repo-wide novelty-vs-anchor advisory cannot localize; (2) GERMLINE vs SOMATIC gate stratification — an edit to the harness propagates to every consumer while an edit to a consumer dies with it, so harness-side gates should be strictly stronger than consumer-side ones, and an unpinned consumer (the posthog/context-mill pattern: one release reshapes the whole fleet's field) is germline editing without a checkpoint
couldBe: the instrument is wrong — the thing that PRODUCED this number, not the thing it describes
both are real and cheap: (1) is mass dims joined against per-component claim counts, already both in status.json; (2) is a policy plus a release-side check that no consumer resolves a floating ref
(1) is noise on a young repo where mass legitimately outruns claims during exploration, and would fire constantly on any greenfield component
shown.discriminatedBy: compute mass-delta vs claim-delta per component over the last N commits on hoist and this repo; if the ratio flags components a human agrees are under-anchored (and stays quiet on ones they agree are fine), it is an instrument; if it flags everything young, it needs a maturity gate before it can ship

shown.chose: unvisited = paths in the recent concern band that the graph does not own — the complement of economy's closure, not a new churn statistic
shown.because: closureOf returns NULL for a commit touching nothing the graph owns, so a path outside the graph can never enter a closure by construction — the two candidate definitions denote the same set and the cheap one reuses fileChurn + the graph's file nodes with no second history read. It measures 173/274 on the consuming project and 72/165 here, which is the finding: most of what recent work touches is invisible to every read-cost figure the harness prints. Denominator is the distinct paths the 2..BULK band touched; with no git it is UNMEASURED, never 0.

shown.chose: index CATCHES Unrunnable from the structural diff and files it as an unread source, instead of letting cli.ts's total handler abort the run
shown.because: cli.ts's total Unrunnable handler is the right answer for a command whose WHOLE JOB needs history (log, signal): it exits 2 with a sentence. The Index has three views and only one of them reads history, so aborting would cost the reader the map and the journal because git was unavailable — a shallow CI clone or a source export is an ordinary consumer, not an exotic state. A pre-check would be floor.ts's rejected shape (a second spelling of the requirement, one per caller). Catching the typed throw keeps the requirement stated once at the seam that discovers it, and the page then says WHICH source it lost and why — which is the same doctrine, applied at a page instead of at a process.
over: letting the CLI's uncaughtException renderer take it, as log and signal do

shown.chose: the default frame is the STORED CURSOR (the prior index.json's head), with the last tag only as a fallback — measured: 'since the last tag' resolves in neither dogfood target
shown.because: QUERY, re-runnable: `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` + `git rev-list --count <tag>..HEAD`. shown.chose: correct the floor's partial-collapse premise in all four places it is spelled, and name the mass measures pin as the mitigation — WITHOUT adding a gate

shown.chose: Fix all three adversarial-review findings rather than accepting any as known limitations, and record in each test's header WHY the gap existed
shown.because: Two fable reviewers found three real defects by mutation, each reproduced in both directions. (1) test/vacuity.test.ts was ITSELF vacuous: both its assertions are universal quantifiers over command output with no check that any command ran, so inserting process.exit(2) after cli.ts's cmd read made both tests pass green — in the one file whose entire subject is instruments that cannot distinguish finding nothing from not looking. The idiom was already in this suite twice (commands.test.ts live.length>=20, and observed.length>=3 in both totality oracles) and simply was not copied. Writing the rule down is not obeying it. (2) claimedFilePaths lost its only witness when scene.test.ts was evicted: mutating it to bless every ambiguous candidate — the exact over-report it exists to prevent — passes 593/593 with verify ✓ coherent, because no spec anchor names it. The asymmetry is the lesson: the UNDER-report direction reds a promise.test.ts assertion, so only the direction that silently inflates a coverage number went dark. (3) artifactSnapshot watched AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/public but not README.md, which docs also writes, so a future root-markdown-only generator would evade the writesArtifacts oracle. THE GENERAL LESSON, which the eviction audit missed: auditing an eviction by TEST COUNT answers arithmetic, not 'was any surviving guarantee ONLY witnessed there'. The second question is the one that bites
over: Deferring the README blind spot because no current generator writes only there
Treating the vacuity oracle's missing instrument check as theoretical, since it only opens when the CLI front door breaks
